THROW-FORWARD: Iris House

By: Laura Byrne | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Iris House Children's Hospice offers a life-line to families living with the isolation and challenge of disabled and terminally ill children. But it is being threatened by drastic budget cuts.

Unique Selling Point:
Iris House founder Sue van der Linde offers extraordinary support to caregivers of children with severe disabilities or terminal illnesses. This free service allows caregivers to leave the house for a few precious hours to attend to errands, while their children are safely in the care of hospice workers. Iris House also provides therapy, social worker support and counselling, and palliative care. It's a vital service for over 670 children - but all this faces an existential threat as national government announces significant cuts to provincial budgets.

Script:


UPSOUND: NOLO: I feel sometimes I wish I can die, man. Because I don't know what must I do. There's no hope, there's no light, there's just dark.
VOICEOVER: In a country with little support for conditions like autism or cerebral palsy, thousands of families struggle with the daily challenge of caring for a disabled child.
UPSOUND: OLIVER'S MOM: I was juggling things, you know, Oliver and the restaurant and our properties and not have any family. Iris House really stepped in for a long time for me.
VOICEOVER: In the Western Cape, one organisation is working to relieve that burden.
UPSOUND: COMMUNITY WORKER: Some of the parents stay with their children, 24 seven. So we give relief. At least the parent must go out and do something else.
UPSOUND: SUE VAN DER LINDE: It's community based respite care. It's all about giving parents a break and giving children the opportunity to have the best quality life that they can.
VOICEOVER: But now this lifeline is under threat. In an upcoming episode of Carte Blanche…
UPSOUND: SUE VAN DER LINDE: It's like a Sword of Damocles hanging over our head right now. We have no idea what the end result is going to be. And that's scary. That's very scary.
VOICEOVER: …as national government struggles to cover its costs in a crumbling economy, budget cuts are taking a devastating toll on organisations like Iris House.
UPSOUND: SUE VAN DER LINDE: The reality is us closing our doors, which cannot happen. It just cannot happen.
VOICEOVER: Will these vulnerable children and their families pay the price?
VOX POP: MOM: I cannot believe that they’re actually going to take it away from our kids.
VOX POP: GRANDMOTHER: They can’t. They must really, people must really get under their skins and tell them exactly, educate them about special needs. Because they don't know much about special needs.
UPSOUND: NOLUBABALO: If they're not around, who am I going to go to? Because I will be lost without Iris House.
UPSOUND: SUE VAN DER LINDE: Parents have, they're already at the edge. Without our services, I'm really concerned that they will go over. And who's going to suffer at the end of the day, it's going to be the children.
